findings.technicalDetail: Brief v1 p. 4 l. 12: 'Harbor delivered the goods on 3 March 2026, two days after the agreed date'. Delivery receipt DR-0931 p. 1 l. 8: 'Delivered: 10 March 2026, 14:20. Received by: J. Okoro'. No document mentions 3 March; the email thread shows Harbor planned to ship on 6 March. The correct date also matters for MSA clause 9.1: rejection on 12 March is two business days after 10 March (inside the five-day window), whereas 3 March would have put it seven business days later. Brief v2 p. 4 l. 12 states 10 March.

proposals.title: Systematic date-assertion sweep across the brief
proposals.researchQuestion: Are there other dates in the brief, beyond the delivery date, that no document in the matter supports?
proposals.motivation: Run #1 checked assertions carrying dates, quantities or party actions and found one unsupported date. A sweep of every date expression gives the lawyer a complete picture before revision.
proposals.hypothesis: H1: the 3 March date is the only unsupported date in brief v1.
proposals.baselineAndControls: Baseline: run #1. Control: every date in the chronology must be found supported by its own source document.
proposals.procedure: Enumerate date expressions in the brief; match each against dated locations in all project documents; report supported / unsupported / ambiguous with page and line.

outcomes.success: H1 holds: exactly one unsupported date.
outcomes.inconclusive: Ambiguous dates that match several documents inconsistently.

recommendations.title: Revise the argument: state the receipt date (10 March 2026) and rely on the clause 9.1 rejection window
recommendations.observedIssue: Brief v1 asserts delivery on 3 March; the signed receipt says 10 March. The wrong date also undermines the rejection-window argument, since 12 March would then be seven business days after delivery.
recommendations.proposedChange: State delivery on 10 March 2026 citing DR-0931 p. 1 l. 8; describe lateness as nine days; present the 12 March rejection as two business days after delivery under MSA clause 9.1.

recommendations.expectedBenefit: Removes a contradiction with Northwind's own signed document and makes the rejection-window argument internally consistent.
tradeOffs: Nine days late reads worse for Harbor but also invites the waiver point (fnd-L-003), which v2 addresses.
applicabilityLimits: Applies to the brief's facts section; the merits are for the lawyer.
